overview: Copart operates the leading online marketplace for salvage and total-loss vehicles, connecting sellers -- primarily insurance companies -- with a global base of buyers (dismantlers, rebuilders, exporters, and dealers) through its proprietary VB3 virtual bidding auction platform. The company owns/operates a network of roughly 250+ vehicle storage and auction facilities (a large land bank) across the U.S., UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, Oman, Ireland and Bahrain, and takes title-transfer or consignment fees on nearly every vehicle that passes through its yards. Copart's core insurance salvage business is a scaled, capital-intensive duopoly with RB Global (IAA) as its only comparable competitor, and in October 2026 it closed its $1.9 billion acquisition of ACV Auctions, pushing the company into mainstream wholesale/non-salvage dealer vehicle remarketing just as it also absorbed a surprise change at the top, with founder Jay Adair returning as CEO in place of Jeff Liaw.

business_model.summary: Copart earns fee-based revenue on essentially every vehicle that moves through its auction platform, primarily under a 'principal' consignment model in which it charges the seller (mostly insurance carriers) a fee for storage, title/DMV processing, transportation and selling services, plus a separate buyer fee paid by the winning bidder. A smaller and more cyclical portion of revenue comes from purchasing vehicles outright (Cash for Cars / CSA / Blue Car programs, wholesale/dealer purchases) and reselling them for its own account, which shows up as 'purchased vehicle' or 'vehicle sales' revenue rather than pure service fee revenue. Because Copart is paid fees regardless of the vehicle's ultimate price (in the standard consignment model), revenue is driven mainly by unit volume (total loss frequency, accident rates, catastrophic weather) and secondarily by average selling price, which affects revenue-share-based fees and purchased-vehicle margins. The newly acquired ACV Auctions adds a transaction-fee-based digital wholesale/dealer-to-dealer vehicle marketplace adjacent to, but distinct from, the salvage model.

revenue_streams.name: Purchased vehicle sales / CSA-Cash for Cars / Blue Car / dealer & wholesale non-insurance
International segment (UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, etc.)
revenue_streams.trend: growing fastest (units +10%, revenue +11.7% in Q4 FY26)

revenue_streams.name: Ancillary services (transportation, title, inspection, Purple Wave construction/ag/fleet auctions) plus newly consolidated ACV Auctions wholesale marketplace
revenue_streams.trend: growing; ACV adds a new, currently sub-scale revenue line post October 2026 close

business_model.customer_type: B2B2C hybrid - sellers are overwhelmingly institutional (insurance carriers ~75-80% of US volume historically, plus dealers, banks, rental/fleet companies, charities); buyers are global, ranging from licensed dismantlers/rebuilders/exporters to the general public; ACV adds a dealer-to-dealer wholesale customer base
business_model.geographic_mix: US the large majority of revenue and profit; International (UK/Europe, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, Oman, Ireland, Bahrain) roughly 20% of revenue in FY2026 but ~38% of units and ~46% of dollars-of-vehicles-sold from international buyers, reflecting Copart's role as an export hub for global used/salvage vehicle demand

competitive_position.market_position: Co-leader of a U.S. salvage-auction duopoly with RB Global's IAA; estimates of Copart's share of the US insurance total-loss salvage market vary widely across sources (roughly 40-65%) with IAA the remainder, and multiple 2026 reports describe share momentum shifting toward IAA for the first time since Copart's early-2000s rise, including on at least one major national carrier (reported to be Progressive)

moat_factors.description: Owning (rather than leasing) a large, geographically dense network of storage/auction yards near major population centers is extremely difficult and slow to replicate, and is critical for responding quickly to catastrophic weather events (hurricanes, wildfires, hail) when insurers need surge capacity

Proprietary online bidding technology and imaging tools created switching costs and efficiency advantages over legacy live-auction models, though IAA/RB Global has closed much of this technology gap in recent years
Scale of buyer base (global dismantlers/exporters) increases auction returns for sellers, reinforcing insurer relationships, while breadth of seller supply attracts more buyers

Multi-year assignment agreements with large national insurers create some stickiness, but carriers can and do reallocate volume between Copart and IAA based on price/service; reports throughout 2026 describe Progressive shifting a larger share of assignments to IAA

Minimal debt (D/E ~0.01) and strong free cash flow generation gave Copart the capital flexibility to fund the entire $1.9B ACV Auctions acquisition from cash on hand without a financing condition, a flexibility few competitors could match

weaknesses: High customer concentration risk: a handful of large national insurers (State Farm, Progressive, Geico, Allstate, etc.) represent an outsized share of US salvage volume, and losing or losing share of a single large account materially moves results

Through FY2026 and into FY2027, Copart has shown signs of losing unit-volume momentum while RB Global/IAA units grew, driven partly by Progressive shifting a greater share of assignments to IAA and IAA's operational cycle-time improvements

Domestic insurance salvage unit growth is maturing/plateauing after a decade of total-loss-frequency-driven growth, pushing Copart to rely more on price and international/non-insurance channels for growth

ACV Auctions (closed October 16, 2026) takes Copart into an adjacent, historically money-losing wholesale marketplace business with integration risk and management's own guidance that the deal is roughly breakeven in year one and not accretive until FY2028

An unexpected CEO change (Jeff Liaw's July 31, 2026 departure and founder Jay Adair's return) adds near-term leadership-transition and strategic-continuity uncertainty on top of the ACV integration, even though the board characterized it as a continuation rather than a reset

growth_drivers: International expansion - UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland and other markets now all profitable, growing units and revenue faster than the US and serving as an export outlet for global used/salvage vehicle demand

Non-insurance seller diversification - dealers, banks, rental/fleet companies, and directly-purchased vehicles via CSA/Cash for Cars/Blue Car programs, reducing reliance on insurance total-loss volume alone

Rising total loss frequency structurally - increasing vehicle repair costs (ADAS, electronics, computer chips) versus used vehicle values continue to push more accident vehicles to salvage rather than repair, a multi-decade secular tailwind though possibly moderating

M&A into adjacent markets - the $1.9B acquisition of ACV Auctions (a digital wholesale/dealer vehicle marketplace), closed October 16, 2026, expands Copart beyond salvage into mainstream used-vehicle wholesale, a large addressable market, with ACV continuing to operate as an independent subsidiary under its existing leadership

Technology/AI investment - management (now under returning CEO Jay Adair) has highlighted AI and automation, international salvage expansion, whole-car salvage in the US, and technology services for customers as strategic priorities
Continued yard/land bank capacity additions to support both catastrophic-event surge capacity and organic volume growth
Pricing/mix - average selling prices rose 3.5% in Q4 FY2026 and 5.5% for full-year FY2026, partially offsetting unit volume softness

business.description: A small number of national insurance carriers drive a large share of US salvage volume; carriers can reallocate business between Copart and IAA/RB Global based on fees, technology, or service levels (e.g., Progressive's 2026 shift toward IAA)

RB Global completed its IAA turnaround; IAA has cut vehicle cycle times and reduced backlog, and 2026 unit growth trends have generally favored IAA over Copart, suggesting the long era of Copart share gains may be reversing

Copart's largest-ever acquisition ($1.9B, closed October 16, 2026) moves it into a new, historically unprofitable wholesale marketplace segment; management guided to breakeven contribution in the first year and accretion not until FY2028

business.risk: Used vehicle price and total loss frequency cyclicality
business.description: Revenue is sensitive to used vehicle values and total loss frequency trends, which can plateau or reverse if repair costs fall relative to vehicle values or if accident rates decline (e.g., improved ADAS/safety features reducing accident frequency over time, or drivers dropping collision coverage)

A meaningful share of volume and revenue upside comes from irregular catastrophic weather events (hurricanes, wildfires, hail storms); results can be lumpy and comparisons distorted by prior-year storm activity

financial.description: Growing international segment (UK, Europe, Brazil, Canada, UAE) creates FX translation exposure on revenue and earnings

Company carries very low leverage (D/E ~0.01) and ample cash/FCF, but the $1.9B ACV deal (funded entirely from cash on hand) reduced the net cash cushion and buyback capacity, at least temporarily, until ACV becomes accretive (guided for FY2028)

regulatory.description: Salvage title laws, end-of-life vehicle recycling rules, and environmental compliance at storage yards vary by state/country and could raise compliance costs

regulatory.risk: Antitrust/competition scrutiny of a two-player market
regulatory.description: The US salvage auction market's duopoly structure (Copart/RB Global) could draw regulatory attention, particularly around further consolidation or exclusive insurer arrangements
Expanding operations across multiple foreign jurisdictions (UK, Germany, Brazil, UAE, etc.) exposes the company to varied local regulatory regimes

macro.description: Higher new vehicle prices and interest rates have historically supported used vehicle values (benefiting Copart's purchased-vehicle margins and fee bases), but a reversal (falling used car prices, easing rates) could pressure average selling prices

macro.risk: Macro/consumer driving activity and insurance affordability
macro.description: Miles driven and accident frequency correlate with economic activity and fuel prices; some reporting in 2026 pointed to drivers dropping collision coverage amid high premiums, which would reduce the pipeline of insured, damaged vehicles reaching salvage auctions
A meaningful share of Copart's buyer base and vehicle value comes from international/export buyers; tariffs, sanctions, or export restrictions in key buyer markets could affect demand and pricing

execution.description: Jeff Liaw stepped down as CEO effective July 31, 2026, roughly two years into his tenure, with founder and former long-tenured CEO Jay Adair returning to the role; the stock fell sharply on the announcement and the move adds leadership-continuity uncertainty on top of the concurrent ACV integration, even though the company stated the change was not related to any disagreement over financial reporting or policy

Jane Pocock (previously UK managing director) was promoted to the newly created President role effective August 1, 2026, extending her operating model globally; successful execution of this restructured leadership team alongside a new CEO and a freshly closed large acquisition is unproven

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global salvage/total-loss vehicle remarketing industry has grown for decades on rising total loss frequency (vehicle repair costs outpacing used vehicle values due to more complex electronics/ADAS), but US unit growth has shown signs of maturing/declining through FY2026 even as international volumes and pricing continue to grow
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - volumes are influenced by miles driven, accident rates, insurance coverage decisions, and catastrophic weather (which can create sharp but temporary spikes), while average selling prices track broader used vehicle market cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect - higher rates have historically supported used vehicle values (benefiting purchased-vehicle margins) but also affect new vehicle affordability and fleet/dealer buying behavior; Copart itself carries minimal debt so direct rate sensitivity on financing costs is low
key_input_costs: Real estate/land (acquisition and carrying cost of the yard network)

recent_developments.event: Copart announced a surprise CEO transition: Jeff Liaw will step down as CEO and director effective July 31, 2026, with founder and former long-tenured CEO (2010-2024) Jay Adair, then Executive Chairman, returning as CEO; the company stated the change was not the result of any disagreement over financial reporting, policies or practices; the stock fell roughly 8% on the news

Copart announced the promotion of Jane Pocock, previously managing director of Copart UK, to the newly created role of President effective August 1, 2026, extending her UK/Ireland operating model group-wide

Copart announced a definitive agreement to acquire ACV Auctions, a digital wholesale used-vehicle marketplace, for approximately $1.9 billion ($10.50/share cash, a ~45% premium to ACV's unaffected price), Copart's largest acquisition ever, to be funded from cash on hand with no financing condition

Q4 FY2026 results (quarter ended July 31, 2026): revenue $1.2B (+2.4% YoY) but gross profit -5.5%, operating income -10.6%, and net income -17.4% YoY; diluted EPS $0.35 vs $0.41 prior year, missing on profitability despite a revenue beat

Copart completed its acquisition of ACV Auctions, ahead of the original year-end-2026 target, after roughly 68.4% of ACV shares were tendered; ACV's NYSE listing was terminated and it now operates as an independent Copart subsidiary under its existing leadership team

CPRT shares fell to a 52-week/multi-year low around $26-27 amid continued concerns over soft US insurance salvage unit volumes, competitive share loss to RB Global/IAA, and uncertainty following the CEO transition and ACV deal; shares subsequently recovered into the low-$30s by mid-November 2026

recent_developments.date: 2026 (through Q3/Q4 FY26 and into Q1 FY27)
recent_developments.event: Competitive dynamic: multiple reports through 2026 described a major national carrier (reported to be Progressive) shifting a larger share of total-loss assignment volume to RB Global's IAA, alongside IAA's operational turnaround (shorter cycle times, reduced backlog); some 2026 commentary also pointed to drivers dropping collision coverage amid high premiums as a separate drag on insured total-loss volumes

International segment strength continued: units sold internationally +10% and international revenue +11.7% in Q4 FY26; international buyers represented ~38% of units and ~46% of dollar volume for the full year, underscoring Copart's role as a global export hub

Copart is scheduled to report Q1 FY2027 results (quarter ended October 31, 2026) on or around November 23, 2026 -- the first full quarterly report to include ACV Auctions post-close and under new CEO Jay Adair; not yet reported as of this analysis

guidance.as_of: Q4 FY2026 Earnings Call (September 10, 2026); no formal update yet from the pending Q1 FY2027 report (expected ~Nov 23, 2026)

items.notes: Management said the deal is expected to be earnings-accretive only starting in FY2028, implying a drag/dilution period through FY2027; this guidance has not yet been updated for the actual October 2026 closing

items.target: Continued elevated total loss frequency expected to persist
items.notes: Management continues to expect the long-term secular trend of rising total loss frequency (driven by repair cost inflation from ADAS/electronics) to continue, even though reported US units declined in FY2026

items.target: Qualitative commitment to continued automation-driven cost reduction
items.notes: Management elevated AI and automation as a top strategic priority for cost efficiency and competitive differentiation, without providing specific quantitative targets

items.target: Growth in international salvage, whole-car salvage in the US, and technology services for customers
items.notes: Returning CEO Jay Adair outlined these as his priority areas upon resuming the role effective July 31, 2026; no specific quantitative targets have been attached yet

guidance.management_commentary: Management framed the Q4 FY2026 miss on gross profit/operating income/net income as reflecting a mix shift and competitive/volume pressure in the US insurance channel, while highlighting record or near-record international growth and profitability across all international markets as evidence the growth algorithm is intact outside the US. Management characterized the ACV Auctions deal as a strategic expansion into the broader wholesale/dealer vehicle marketplace adjacent to its core salvage business, acknowledging it would be roughly breakeven in year one with accretion expected by FY2028. Separately, upon returning as CEO in July 2026, Jay Adair indicated his near-term focus areas as international salvage growth, whole-car salvage in the US, and technology services for customers; the Q1 FY2027 earnings call (expected ~Nov 23, 2026) should be the first opportunity for the new CEO and President Jane Pocock to update guidance with ACV now consolidated.

bull_case: Duopoly market structure with a scaled, hard-to-replicate land bank of auction/storage yards provides durable competitive advantage and pricing power over the long run

International segment (UK, Germany, Brazil, Canada, UAE, Spain, Finland, etc.) is now profitable in all markets and growing units/revenue faster than the US, providing a second growth engine and export demand outlet

Secular total-loss-frequency tailwind remains intact structurally as vehicles become more expensive to repair (ADAS, electronics) relative to their value, supporting long-term volume growth even if near-term US trends are soft

Extremely strong balance sheet (D/E ~0.01) let Copart fund the entire $1.9B ACV Auctions acquisition from cash on hand with no financing condition, and the deal expands Copart's addressable market into mainstream wholesale/dealer vehicle remarketing, a much larger market than salvage alone

The return of founder Jay Adair as CEO, backed by 14 years of prior Copart leadership (2010-2024) and a newly created President role under Jane Pocock, could be read as a stabilizing, execution-focused move by the board rather than a sign of deeper problems, and shares have already recovered from their October 2026 lows
Shares trade well off 52-week highs (down roughly 30%+ over the trailing year as of November 2026) which, if competitive and integration concerns prove overdone, offers valuation support
bear_case: Through 2026, Copart has shown signs of losing unit-volume momentum and share to a resurgent RB Global/IAA, which has closed operational gaps (cycle times, backlog) and is reportedly winning incremental insurer assignment volume (e.g., a Progressive shift), challenging the thesis of an unassailable moat

Q4 FY2026 results showed a meaningful profitability miss (gross profit -5.5%, operating income -10.6%, net income -17.4% YoY) despite a revenue beat, suggesting margin/mix pressure in the core US business, and some reporting points to drivers dropping collision coverage as a structural drag on insured total-loss volumes

ACV Auctions, now closed, is Copart's largest-ever acquisition at $1.9B into a historically unprofitable, unproven-at-scale adjacent business, with management itself guiding to breakeven (not accretive) contribution through FY2027 and integration risk given ACV's separate leadership and technology stack

The unplanned July 2026 CEO transition (Liaw out, Adair back in after only ~2 years under Liaw) adds leadership-continuity and strategy-execution uncertainty at the same time the company is digesting its largest-ever acquisition, a combination that unsettled the market and drove an 8% one-day stock decline on the announcement

US domestic insurance salvage volumes appear to be plateauing/declining, meaning future growth increasingly depends on pricing, international expansion, and non-insurance sellers rather than the core secular driver that fueled the past decade's growth

Despite a roughly 30%+ decline over the trailing year into November 2026, the stock still carries a premium multiple reflecting its historical best-in-class moat and growth, leaving little room for error if competitive share losses, margin compression, CEO-transition disruption, or ACV integration issues persist
